In Unity3D, if you want a GameObject **NOT** to receive touch (or click/mouse) events, you generally want that object to **ignore user input** such as `IPointerClickHandler` or avoid it being selected by raycasts. There are several ways to achieve this, depending on what kind of object it is (UI or 3D) and how your input logic works.

## For UI (using UnityEngine.UI)

If your GameObject is a UI element (e.g., `Image`, `Button`, etc):

### 1. Remove/Disable Raycast Target

- Uncheck the `Raycast Target` property on the `Image` or `Text` component.  
  This makes the UI element invisible to all UI EventSystems.

### 2. Canvas Group - Blocks Raycasts
- Add a `CanvasGroup` component to the UI element.
- Set `Blocks Raycasts` to **false**.

This will make it, and its children, completely ignore any UI interactions.

**Example:**
```csharp
gameObject.GetComponent<CanvasGroup>().blocksRaycasts = false;
```

---

## For 3D Objects (Colliders)

If your object has a Collider (for 3D Raycasting):

### 1. Remove/Disable the Collider

- The easiest way: **Remove or Disable the Collider** component:
```csharp
gameObject.GetComponent<Collider>().enabled = false;
```
This way, it cannot be picked up by raycasts.

### 2. Use a Layer Mask

You can control which GameObjects receive raycast hits by placing this GameObject on a layer **not included in your input LayerMask**.

**Example (when raycasting):**
```csharp
// Suppose you want to ignore the "IgnoreTouch" layer
int layerMask = ~(1 << LayerMask.NameToLayer("IgnoreTouch"));

if (Physics.Raycast(ray, out hit, 100, layerMask))
{
    // This will not hit "IgnoreTouch" layer GameObjects
}
```

### 3. Custom Touch Logic
If you use your own touch or click handling (e.g. by checking what's under the finger/cursor), simply **ignore** this object in your logic (e.g., by tag, layer, or some custom flag).

---

## Summary Table

| Object Type | How to Ignore Touch Events                          |
|-------------|:---------------------------------------------------|
| UI          | Disable Raycast Target/CanvasGroup.blocksRaycasts   |
| 3D Object   | Remove/Disable Collider or Layer Mask filtering     |

---

## TL;DR

> **UI:** Set `blocksRaycasts = false` on a CanvasGroup, or uncheck `Raycast Target` on UI components.  
> **3D:** Disable Collider, or exclude the object's layer in raycast LayerMask.
